source.name: IDM and experimental electronic
source.lineage: Early-1990s onward experimental-electronic genre intentionally constructed for headphone listening rather than club-dance use, characterized by complex broken-beat programming, glitchy textural sound design, and the post-acid-house compositional ambition — codified through Aphex Twin (Selected Ambient Works 85-92 in 1992, Richard D. James Album 1996), Autechre (Tri Repetae 1995), Boards of Canada (Music Has the Right to Children 1998), Squarepusher, the Warp Records Artificial Intelligence series

extras.description: IDM / Intelligent Dance Music (codified 1992 onward, named for the Hyperreal IDM mailing list and crystallizing through Warp Records' Artificial Intelligence series — Aphex Twin, Autechre, Black Dog Productions, B12), the listening-rather-than-dancing electronic music genre. Defined by intricately-programmed beat construction often using complex polyrhythms and microtimings impossible for human-drummers, microtonal-and-detuned pitch design rejecting equal-temperament defaults, ambient-and-pad textural foundations underlying the rhythmic foreground, song-form built on long-form sectional development rather than dance-floor-functional vamp construction, and home-listening-oriented (album-format, headphone-aware) production aesthetic. Subgenres include Braindance (Rephlex label specialty), drill-and-bass (extreme-fast Squarepusher-Aphex Twin style), and ambient-IDM. Distinguished from straight techno or house by absence of dance-floor functionality; distinguished from ambient by retention of rhythmic-pulse foreground; distinguished from glitch (later subgenre) by greater commitment to song-form structure.

source.name: Microhouse
source.lineage: Berlin-and-Cologne minimal-techno genre extending Chicago-house's rhythmic foundation through clicks-and-cuts micro-detail textural aesthetic and Kompakt-label-associated restrained-palette arrangement — codified through Akufen (My Way 2002), Matthew Herbert, Ricardo Villalobos (Alcachofa 2003, Fizheuer Zieheuer 2006), Luciano, Magda, with the genre serving as the early-2000s Cologne-Berlin minimal-aesthetic mainstream

extras.description: Microhouse / minimal house (codified 2002-2005 through Cologne's Kompakt label and Berlin's Perlon label scenes, descending from minimal-techno and Cologne's earlier dub-techno lineage), the minimal-techno-influenced house subgenre. Defined by sparse arrangement built on clicks-and-cuts foley-and-percussive-fragment textures (the genre's signature aesthetic of using small environmental sound samples as percussion), repurposed micro-sample foundations rather than traditional house drum-machine-and-synth palette, four-on-floor kick foundation with sparse hi-hats and percussion programmed at quiet dynamic levels, atmospheric-pad textures filling the harmonic space, and tempo around 122-126 BPM. Album-format release lineage (Pole, Akufen, Matthew Dear early productions) over single-track-DJ-format. Distinguished from straight house by minimal arrangement and micro-sample foreground; distinguished from minimal techno by retention of house tempo and mid-tempo groove; distinguished from dub techno (its ancestor) by absence of long-decay chord-pad foreground.

extras.description: Peak-time techno (codified 1990s onward through Berlin's Tresor and London's Lost club residencies, with continuous tradition through to present), the hard-fast club-floor techno subgenre. source.name: Stutter House
source.lineage: Late-1990s European house production technique-turned-microstyle in which a short vocal or chord sample is retriggered in sixteenth- and thirty-second-note bursts across a straight 124-128 BPM four-on-the-floor, developed out of Paris filter-house and Dutch/Italian club edits by producers working on Akai samplers and early Cubase, with resonant filter sweeps, sidechain-pumped bass and long looped disco-source stabs.

extras.description: Stutter house names the family of late-1990s and 2000s house records built around aggressively retriggered sample fragments — a syllable, a chord stab or a snare rush repeated in machine-gun subdivisions against an otherwise plain four-on-the-floor. The technique is a sampler artefact made into a hook, usually combined with filter sweeps and hard sidechain compression inherited from French touch. It differs from filter house proper, which loops a whole disco bar untouched, and from later vocal-chop EDM by keeping the source recognisable and the arrangement DJ-tool sparse.
exemplars: Thomas Bangalter — Trax on da Rocks
Stardust — Music Sounds Better with You
Armand Van Helden — U Don't Know Me

source.name: Classic Trance

extras.description: Classic trance is the mid-1990s German template that established the genre's architecture: a 135-142 BPM kick with sixteenth-note offbeat bass, sequenced arpeggios in a minor key, a filtered pad breakdown lasting a minute or more, and a snare-roll release into a euphoric detuned lead.
